Dr. Howard is undoubtedly one of the best instructors in Bilkent. He has no weak points at all. He’s very thoughtful, kind, and incredibly student friendly. He always asks for students’ opinions on things, and he’s very open to feedback. He sends us class summaries after each class, and does his best to ensure we’re being informed about what’s going on in the class. He’s encouraging student participation all the time. His assessments make perfect sense in the context of this course. In the final, I was amazed at just how fun and interesting an essay question was. Writing journals to keep record of our most interesting thoughts is an amazing idea. If you pick Dr. Howard, as your instructor, be aware that you will be asked to produce original ideas in a regular manner, rather than to memorize everything for a midterm. He promotes critical thinking rather than memorization. I’ve noticed one thing in his class: everyone performs better with Dr. Howard because they feel more involved in the class, and are drawn to the course by Dr. Howard’s focus on the most thought-provoking things in the books, and the connections he makes with other media, or the historical context. Strongest Points of the Instructor: The instructor's strongest qualities lie in the wide range of project options offered demonstrates a strong commitment to catering to diverse student interests. The inclusion of participation opportunities through letter of participation, is another commendable aspect, as it encourages students who may not feel comfortable speaking in class to engage with the course in meaningful ways.


Weakest Points of the Instructor : Despite these strengths, the instructor's approach has notable weaknesses. The expectation for entirely novel and groundbreaking ideas can be unrealistic and overwhelming for students, particularly when the instructor's extensive experience makes it difficult to present something truly new in their eyes. This focus on originality, without examples of successful projects, can leave students feeling lost despite putting in significant effort. Additionally, this rigidity may unintentionally discourage students who excel in effort, or practical application but struggle to meet the high standard of uniqueness. The instructor’s deep familiarity with the subject may also lead to a disconnect from the challenges students face in navigating such demanding expectations. The instructor’s approach to grading open-ended questions also feels excessively harsh at times. Since these types of questions often do not have a clear number of reasons or specific structure required for a complete answer, cutting entire points—or even half points—can seem overly cruel and disheartening to students who made an earnest attempt.

Strongest Aspects of the Course: One of the strongest aspects of the course is its focus on introducing students to ancient literary works such as the Iliad and Epic of Gilgamesh (while I personally didn’t enjoy Gilgamesh). These texts not only provide historical cultures but also foster an appreciation for the origins of literature and storytelling

Weakest Aspects of the Course: Despite these strengths, the course has significant weaknesses. As an engineering student, I found the workload and expectations to be disproportionately demanding compared to some of my core technical subjects, such as Electrical Engineering (EEE) and Mathematics lectures. My friends and I often struggled to keep up with the course requirements, as the effort needed to analyze and interpret the material was far greater than anticipated. Even after dedicating substantial time and effort, I frequently felt that my hard work was not adequately rewarded. This disconnect between effort and reward made the course feel more burdensome than enriching. Greater flexibility in grading and a more balanced workload would make the course more approachable and rewarding for students from non-humanities backgrounds.
As an engineering student, I am glad that this course exists since it enables me to improve myself intellectualy, and do not depend only on the engineering courses.
